Aligned for Ascent
Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Limited (ARE&M) has evolved considerably 
over the last few years. While our Lead Acid Battery business continues 
to hold a strong position across automotive and industrial applications, 
the business today extends beyond its traditional areas of operation. 
Investments in battery packs, cell technologies, energy storage solutions, 
recycling and power electronics have broadened our presence across the 
energy and mobility landscape.
FY 2025-26 was a year of progress across several important initiatives. Work continued on the Customer 
Qualification Plant, e+ Energy Labs and the Giga Cell project, each of which represents a different part of our 
New Energy roadmap. At the same time, our established businesses remained focused on market execution, 
manufacturing efficiency, product quality and customer service. 
This is particularly important at a time when 
energy and mobility markets are undergoing 
structural change. Customer requirements 
are evolving, technology cycles are becoming 
shorter and new applications are creating fresh 
opportunities across industries. Responding 
to these developments requires more than 
investment alone. It requires the ability to 
translate ideas into products, products into 
operations and operations into commercially 
viable businesses.
The progress made over recent years has 
placed us in a stronger position to do exactly 
that. We enter the period ahead with greater 
manufacturing depth, wider technology 
capabilities, an expanding New Energy portfolio 
and a clear understanding of where we intend 
to participate.
The theme of this report, ‘Aligned for Ascent’, 
reflects this stage of our evolution. It captures 
the growing connection between our businesses, 
investments and capabilities, and our readiness 
to pursue the opportunities emerging across 
energy and mobility markets.To us is proactively rebelling 
for better ways of doing 
things leading to newer 
possibilities 
To us is leading with courage 
and conviction to convert 
gaps into opportunities, 
create wealth and contribute 
to growth
To us is the total ownership of our thoughts and actions in 
every situation to achieve maximum common good in the 
best interest of the Environment, Society, Customer, Supplier, 
Employee & ShareholdersTo us is continually 
enhancing our performance 
to consistently produce 
outstanding results with 
lasting impactThrough the Amara Raja Way and 
through enduring progressive 
partnerships we will be a Global Leader in 
Energy & Mobility Solutions.
To transform our increasing spheres of 
influence and to improve the quality of 
life by building institutions that provide 
better access to better opportunities to 
more people... 
All the time…

our stakeholders, which

something special, leading 
to endearing relationshipsInnovation...

preferred brands across the world. 
This momentum is powered by our strong distribution backbone, trusted 
product performance and a growing portfolio that includes next-gen lithium 
battery packs and EV charging solutions. As we grow our footprint in new 
geographies and adjacent businesses, we remain focused on delivering value 
with agility, foresight and responsibility.

technologies. The business moved from industrial batteries to 
automotive batteries, premium brands, international markets and, 
more recently, new energy businesses. Each phase introduced

Chairman and Managing Director's Letter
The global energy 
landscape may continue 
to shift, but Amara Raja’s 
readiness shaped by legacy, 
strengthened by innovation, 
and aligned with India’s ascent 
positions us for sustained, 
transformative growth.
Dear Shareholders,
It fills me with a deep sense 
of pride that in the financial 
year 2025–26, our organisation 
has navigated one of the most 
complex global environments 
of recent times. This year 
demanded agility, foresight, 
discipline, and most of all 
resilience, not just from 
businesses worldwide, but 
from nations and institutions 
reshaping their economic and 
energy futures. And yet, amid 
these uncertainties, Amara Raja 
continued to perform steadily. Volatility was the hallmark of most 
world economies even as geopolitical 
tensions, prolonged conflicts, and 
shifting alliances disrupted energy 
flows and trade routes. Elevated 
interest rates in major economies, 
stubborn inflation, and uneven demand 
recovery created an unpredictable 
global industrial landscape. Meanwhile, 
supply chains for critical minerals like 
lithium, cobalt, nickel, and rare earths 
remained concentrated in vulnerable 
geographies, sharpening the urgency 
for energy sovereignty. Countries 
accelerated clean energy deployment, 
but gaps in storage, grid readiness, 
and technology access persisted, 
intensifying competition for advanced 
chemistry cell technologies and energy 
storage leadership.In sharp contrast, India emerged as 
one of the world’s most resilient growth 
engines. Supported by robust domestic 
consumption, strong macroeconomic 
fundamentals, and policy stability, the 
country demonstrated remarkable 
economic momentum. Continued 
investments in infrastructure, 
industrial corridors, renewable energy 
capacity, and ‘Make in India’ initiatives 
strengthened India’s position as a 
reliable global manufacturing and 
energy transition hub. The country’s 
relentless push toward self reliance 
particularly in electronics, mobility, 
battery technologies, and advanced 
manufacturing aligned closely with the 
long term aspirations of the energy and 
mobility sector.It is against this macroeconomic 
backdrop that Amara Raja’s journey 
this year truly reflects our legacy of 
transformation, resilience, and forward 
thinking. From our inception as a 
challenger in the lead-acid battery 
space to our evolution into a diversified 
energy and mobility leader, Amara 
Raja has always risen step by step, 
opportunity by opportunity guided 
by innovation, values, and a deep 
commitment to nation building.
This year marked a continuation of that 
upward trajectory. In our core lead acid 
battery business, we reinforced market 
leadership through deeper customer 
engagement, product quality, and 
operational excellence. Even as global 
headwinds weighed on other markets, 
India’s manufacturing dynamism and 
expanding mobility landscape helped 
us deliver solid performance across 
business lines. The Indian lead acid 
market remains resilient, supported 
by stable automotive replacement 
demand, robust inverter and HUPS 
usage, and widespread reliance on 
dependable power backup solutions 
across households, SMEs, and essential 
services. 
At the same time, we accelerated 
our pivot to the new energy future, 
a transformative journey that will 
define the next era of Amara Raja. 
The development of our Giga 
Corridor, progress on our lithium 
ion cell manufacturing facility, and 
the foundation stone laying of our 
Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) 
assembly plant stand as milestones in 
this ascent. These initiatives are not 
merely expansions, they are strategic 
investments aligned with India’s vision 
for energy security, reduced import 
dependence, and world class storage 
infrastructure.Grid modernisation, renewable 
integration, and the rise of electric 
mobility are reshaping how nations 
think about energy resilience. 
BESS is becoming central to this 
transformation, and Amara Raja is 
positioning itself at the forefront 
leveraging decades of expertise in 
electrochemistry, manufacturing, 
systems integration, and customer 
centric engineering.
For exports - particularly markets 
such as the US, faced tariff related 
pressure, geopolitical uncertainty, 
and intensifying global competition, 
which moderated volumes and created 
margin headwinds. Despite this, we 
continued to consolidate our position 
through disciplined execution and 
strong customer engagement. 
We strengthened our sustainability 
performance – improving our S&P 
Global Corporate Sustainability 
Assessment score, ranking #1 in India, 
#2 in Asia-Pacific, and #5 globally in 
our sector. We also achieved a CDP 
Climate rating of ‘A-’ in our maiden 
Water Disclosure and became a 
signatory to the WASH initiative. During 
the year, we launched the Vitality 
Index initiative to promote preventive 
healthcare and active lifestyles among 
employees.
Our journey has taught us 
that industries evolve in cycles, 
technologies transform landscapes, 
and organisations thrive when they 
anticipate the future rather than 
react to it. As global corporations 
recalibrated supply chains, India 
became a preferred destination for 
scalable, reliable, innovation-led 
manufacturing. Similarly, Amara 
Raja’s own evolution this year reflects 
a company preparing not just to 
participate in India’s growth story, but 
to shape it.As we enter the next phase of our 
journey, we do so with optimism, 
clarity, and conviction. The global 
energy landscape may continue to 
shift, but Amara Raja’s readiness 
shaped by legacy, strengthened by 
innovation, and aligned with India’s 
ascent positions us for sustained, 
transformative growth.
Together, we will continue to rise - 
purposefully, responsibly, and boldly 
- toward a future where Amara Raja 
plays an even more integral role in 
powering India’s energy and mobility 
ambitions.
To our shareholders, I extend my 
deepest appreciation for your 
continued trust and support during 
this exciting period of transformation. 
To our customers, we are grateful for 
choosing Amara Raja as your partner 
in energy solutions. I extend my 
appreciation to our employees whose 
dedication, innovation and unwavering 
commitment to excellence drives us 
forward. I also thank our partners, 
suppliers, and insurers for supporting 
us as we work together to build a 
stronger and more sustainable future.
The road ahead presents equal 
measures of opportunity and challenge. 
Thank you for your continued support 
and confidence in Amara Raja Energy 
and Mobility. 
Warm regards,
Jayadev Galla 
Chairman and Managing Director 
Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Limited
Jayadev Galla
Chairman and 
Managing Director

Message from Executive Director - 
Automotive and Industrial Business
Together with our 
partners, customers, and 
stakeholders, we are 
confident of building a 
stronger, more resilient, and 
technology-driven future.
Harshavardhana Gourineni
Executive Director 
Automotive and Industrial
Dear Shareholders,
FY 2025-26 has been a year of 
resilient growth, disciplined
execution and strategic 
transformation for Amara Raja 
Energy & Mobility Limited. 
Amid global uncertainties, 
supply chain disruptions and 
cost pressures, we continued
to strengthen our market 
leadership while building 
a future-ready, technology 
driven enterprise.The Indian lead-acid battery market, 
valued at approximately USD 5 billion 
continues to be a stable and reliable 
engine for the broader energy ecosystem. 
Our core automotive and industrial 
businesses delivered robust performance 
during the year, supported by strong 
demand across OEM and replacement 
segments. We achieved 12% revenue 
growth, reflecting sustained momentum 
across key product categories in domestic 
market. 
Our lubricants business in domestic 
market emerged as a high-growth 
vertical, delivering more that 30% revenue 
growth, reinforcing our strategy of 
building complementary adjacencies. We 
continued to strengthen our technology-
led portfolio through the launch of advanced products, including AGM 
(Absorbent Glass Mat) and EFB (Enhanced 
Flooded Batteries) batteries, new-
generation home UPS systems, tubular 
batteries, and solar solutions. These 
initiatives position us strongly to address 
evolving mobility and energy storage 
requirements. 
Our OEM business further deepened its 
partnerships with leading automotive 
manufacturers, earning multiple quality, 
delivery, and sustainability awards from 
marquee customers. These recognitions 
underscore our commitment to 
operational excellence and customer trust. 
From an industrial business perspective, 
we reinforced our leadership across key 
segments. We maintained leadership position in telecom segment, while 
powering over 50,000 telecom towers 
with lithium-ion solutions, building a 
cumulative 1 GWh installation base over 
the last two years. We also strengthened 
our presence in UPS, manufacturing, and 
data centre segments, gaining market 
share in a rapidly transitioning C&I 
landscape, while expanding into high-
growth areas such as renewable energy, 
BESS, and motive applications. 
Operational excellence remained at the 
core of our strategy. Over 100 Quality 
Circle teams achieved national and 
international recognition, reflecting deep 
employee engagement and a strong 
culture of continuous improvement. Our 
manufacturing network expanded with 
new OEM programs and international 
business wins, alongside large-scale 
export execution and process innovations. 
We also made significant progress in 
global expansion. Our international 
business extended its footprint to 70+ 
countries, while retaining leadership 
positions across key markets in the 
Middle East and Asia. Strategic initiatives 
such as the establishment of a regional 
headquarters in Dubai, entry into 
new geographies, and key global 
partnerships further strengthened our 
global competitiveness. A major area of 
focus during the year was supply chain 
transformation and resilience. Through 
focused initiatives across procurement, 
logistics, and distribution, we delivered 
substantial value creation: 
	 Delivered strong procurement 
efficiencies through sourcing, 
localization, and supplier 
consolidation. 
	 Enhanced supply resilience by 
localizing critical materials and 
simplifying the supplier base. 
	 Improved logistics efficiency 
through freight optimisation and 
reduced transit losses. 
Our circular economy initiatives also 
gained scale, with 1.49 Lakh metric 
tonnes of scrap collected through our battery waste management ecosystem, 
reinforcing our commitment to 
sustainability and responsible resource 
management. 
Digital transformation continued to be 
a key enabler across the enterprise. We 
accelerated the deployment of Industry 
4.0 technologies, including IoT-enabled 
systems, real-time analytics, AI-driven 
dashboards, and vision-based quality 
systems, significantly improving 
productivity, quality, and decision 
making. 
Enterprise-wide digital platforms 
such as Dealer Management Systems, 
procurement digitization through 
ARIBA, and advanced analytics have 
enhanced visibility, governance, and 
operational efficiency. 
Our ‘Factory of the Future’ initiatives 
and capacity expansion programs 
have further strengthened our 
manufacturing competitiveness. 
Capacity enhancements under the 
Amara Raja Operating Systems (AROS) 
initiative have further strengthened our 
ability to scale, with installed capacity 
reaching 25 million four-wheeler and 
45  million two-wheeler units.
Sustainability remains central to our 
strategy. During FY 2025-26, we 
maintained Zero Liquid Discharge 
across all manufacturing facilities, 
sustained 12X Water Positivity, signed 
the WASH Pledge, recycled over 99% 
of waste generated, and increased 
recycled lead and lead alloy usage to 
88.27% of total input materials. Our 67 
MW captive renewable energy capacity 
helped avoid approximately 72,790 
tonnes of CO₂ emissions, advancing 
our decarbonisation roadmap. 
Safety and employee well-being 
remained non-negotiable, with 
zero fatalities across operations and 
continued strengthening of our safety 
culture through focused governance, 
leadership commitment, capability 
building, and critical risk management. 
Beyond the workplace, we trained over 
8,500 employees in defensive driving to 
promote road safety.We assessed 87% of our supplier base 
by purchase value on sustainability 
parameters, fostering alignment with 
the Sustainable Development Goals 
(SDGs). We also launched the Vitality 
Index (VI) Programme, achieving 
98.8% coverage of annual medical 
examinations for employees.
Looking ahead, we remain committed 
to deeper sustainability integration 
through increased renewable energy 
adoption, value chain decarbonisation, 
Life Cycle Assessments (LCA), 
implementation of a Biodiversity 
Management Plan, and greater 
digitalization to enhance occupational 
health and safety performance.
With a strong domestic foundation, 
an expanding international presence, 
a future-ready manufacturing 
ecosystem, and an unwavering focus 
on sustainability, Amara Raja is well 
positioned to navigate challenges and 
capitalise on emerging opportunities 
in the evolving energy and mobility 
landscape. 
Together with our partners, customers, 
and stakeholders, we are confident of 
building a stronger, more resilient, and 
technology-driven future. 
Thank you for your continued trust and 
support.
Warm regards,
Harshavardhana Gourineni  
Executive Director  
Automotive and Industrial

Message from Executive Director - 
New Energy Business
Our investments across 
research, testing, 
manufacturing, battery 
management systems, pack 
integration, and system 
engineering are intended to 
ensure that we remain agile 
as technology pathways 
continue to evolve.
Dear Shareholders,
Over the last several years, 
we have consistently 
articulated our ambition of 
transforming Amara Raja 
into a diversified Energy & 
Mobility enterprise. The past 
year marks an important 
shift in that journey — from 
strategy, communication, 
and capability building to 
operational execution. Across our New Energy business, 
multiple foundational projects are 
now moving from development into 
production and commercialisation. 
We have been operating battery pack 
assembly facilities across a range 
of low-voltage applications and 
continue to expand both capability 
and customer engagement. This has 
culminated in cumulative lithium 
battery pack installations exceeding  
1 GWh in the telecom sector alone. 
Consistent with our long-term 
roadmap, the current year will see the 
commissioning of e+ Energy Labs, our 
advanced research and engineering centre, alongside the Customer 
Qualification Plant (CQP), formally 
marking our entry into domestic 
lithium-ion cell manufacturing. We 
are set to begin shipping commercial 
samples to our customers over the 
next couple of months. In parallel, we 
are accelerating the development of 
our Battery Energy Storage System 
(BESS) integration facility, with start 
of production targeted later this year 
at a capacity of 10 GWh. Our first 
gigafactory also remains on track to 
commence production next year. 
The vision of the Amara Raja Giga 
Corridor is now steadily taking shape as envisaged — an integrated ecosystem 
spanning advanced research, a 
committed cell manufacturing 
footprint of 16 GWh, pack assembly, 
battery management systems, and 
complex energy and mobility solutions 
integration. 
What we once referred to as “New 
Energy” is no longer confined to 
emerging applications alone. While 
electric mobility and grid-scale energy 
storage remain major long term growth 
drivers, advanced battery chemistries 
are increasingly finding relevance 
across conventional applications 
such as telecom infrastructure, UPS 
systems, industrial power reliability, 
and over time, potentially even 
selective automotive SLI applications. 
This transition reinforces our belief 
that the future of energy storage will 
not be defined by a single chemistry 
or application, but by the ability 
to intelligently deploy appropriate 
technologies across diverse use cases. 
At Amara Raja, we are therefore 
taking an open and application-led 
approach to chemistry development 
and integration. This is not a passive 
strategy. Our investments across 
research, testing, manufacturing, 
battery management systems, pack 
integration, and system engineering 
are intended to ensure that we 
remain agile as technology pathways 
continue to evolve. We are building a 
deep capability platform that ensures 
our core automotive and industrial 
businesses remain future-ready, 
while simultaneously securing early 
leadership positions in next-generation 
applications. Even amidst continuing 
geopolitical uncertainty and global 
market volatility, we remain focused on 
disciplined execution and long-term 
capability creation. This flexibility is especially important 
in the current global environment. 
Geopolitical disruptions, supply 
chain realignments, and energy 
market volatility continue to reshape 
investment priorities worldwide. 
While the Energy Transition remains a 
powerful long-term structural trend, 
recent disruptions have elevated 
Energy Security into an immediate 
national priority for many countries. 
Nations are increasingly prioritising the 
resilience, localisation, and strategic 
security of their energy ecosystems. 
In this environment, Battery Energy 
Storage Systems have emerged as a 
particularly strategic segment, enabling 
more effective utilisation of renewable 
energy, improving grid reliability, 
strengthening industrial resilience, 
and supporting broader resource 
sovereignty objectives. We see this as 
a defining opportunity. While electric 
mobility will continue to be a major 
long-term demand driver for advanced 
cells, the rapid acceleration of energy 
storage deployments globally is 
reshaping the near-term trajectory of 
the sector. 
We believe we are operating at the 
critical intersection of Energy Transition 
and Energy Security — two themes 
that are increasingly reinforcing one 
another. This convergence creates a 
significant opportunity for integrated 
energy companies capable of 
delivering reliable, scalable, and locally 
anchored solutions that help reduce 
our dependence on foreign energy 
resources. 
Our strategy therefore continues to 
focus on building such an integrated 
platform. We are investing across the 
value chain — from cell development 
and manufacturing to packs, battery 
management systems, energy storage integration, and recycling – 
while simultaneously strengthening 
partnerships, localisation efforts, and 
supply chain resilience. Even amidst 
continuing geopolitical uncertainty 
and global market volatility, we remain 
focused on disciplined execution and 
long-term capability creation. 
The progress achieved over the last 
year would not have been possible 
without the continued support of our 
employees, customers, partners, policy 
makers, shareholders, and broader 
stakeholders. 
Together, we are building not only 
a stronger Amara Raja, but also 
contributing towards a more resilient, 
energy-secure, and self-reliant future 
for India.

DISCUSSION  
AND ANALYSIS
The Management Discussion and Analysis of Amara 
Raja Energy & Mobility Limited has been prepared in 
compliance with Regulation 34(2)(e) read with Schedule 
V (Part B) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015. This section presents an 
overview of the Company’s business performance, industry 
developments and outlook.Global Economy Overview1 
The global economy maintained stable 
growth momentum during CY 2025, 
with global GDP growth estimated at 
approximately 3.4%, broadly in line 
with the previous year despite rising 
geopolitical tensions, evolving trade 
policies and persistent macroeconomic 
uncertainty. Emerging market and 
developing economies continued 
to outperform with growth of 4.4%, 
reinforcing their role as key contributors 
to global economic expansion, while 
advanced economies registered 
relatively moderate growth of 1.9%. 
Global inflation remained broadly stable 
at 4.1%, although inflationary trends 
continued to vary across regions amid 
higher energy prices, commodity market 
volatility and differentiated monetary 
policy responses. Financial markets also 
witnessed fluctuations in bond yields, 
currencies and equity markets reflecting 
shifting investor sentiment and evolving 
macroeconomic conditions globally.
Global industrial activity remained 
mixed during the year as 
manufacturing output in several 
regions faced pressure from elevated 
input costs, cautious consumer 
spending and higher financing 
costs. However, sectors linked to 
electrification, renewable energy 
integration, mobility solutions, 
electronics, telecom infrastructure, 
AI-led digital infrastructure and 
industrial automation continued to 
witness healthy investment momentum 
globally. Rising investments in energy 
storage solutions, advanced battery 
technologies and clean mobility 
ecosystems continued to support 
industrial demand, while increasing 
focus on localisation, resilient supply 
chains and diversification of global 
manufacturing bases remained key 
structural trends shaping industrial 
growth. At the same time, volatility in 
crude oil, metals, rare earths and critical 
mineral supply chains continued to 
influence procurement strategies and 
industrial cost structures across sectors.Key Trends
	 Rising investments in electrification, renewable energy integration, energy 
storage systems, mobility solutions and AI-led infrastructure accelerated 
demand for advanced industrial and battery technologies globally.
	 Increasing policy focus on localisation, clean mobility, energy security and 
diversification of manufacturing ecosystems continued to reshape global 
supply chains and industrial investments.
	 Elevated geopolitical tensions, disruptions across critical energy supply routes 
and volatility in crude oil, metals and rare earth supply chains continued to 
impact global trade flows, logistics costs and industrial procurement strategies

North America
North America continued to 
demonstrate relative economic 
resilience during the year. The US

and is projected to grow by 2.3% in

CY 2027. Inflation in the United States 
remained elevated, with core personal 
consumption expenditure inflation 
at 3.1%. Technology-led investments, 
resilient consumer spending and 
improving business activity supported 
growth despite higher interest rates 
and policy uncertainties.
Middle East & Africa
The Middle East & Africa region 
witnessed elevated macroeconomic 
volatility due to geopolitical tensions, 
energy market disruptions and 
inflationary pressures. The ongoing 
conflict and supply-side disruptions 
intensified financial vulnerabilities 
across commodity-importing 
economies, while higher energy 
prices and tighter financial conditions 
continued to impact regional economic 
activity and trade flows. Central America
Central America witnessed moderate 
economic activity amid elevated global 
uncertainty, tighter financial conditions 
and ongoing geopolitical disruptions 
impacting global trade and commodity

supported by resilient domestic 
consumption, tourism recovery and 
remittance inflows, while inflationary 
pressures and external vulnerabilities 
continued to pose challenges for 
import-dependent economies
Southeast Asia
Southeast Asian economies continued 
to benefit from supply chain

Oceania
Oceania maintained relatively stable 
economic momentum supported by

tensions and evolving global

OUTLOOK
The global economy is projected to grow by around 3.1% in CY 2026, while global inflation is expected to remain 
elevated at 4.4% reflecting the impact of higher energy prices, tighter financial conditions and continued geopolitical 
fragmentation. Global trade growth is expected to moderate compared to elevated levels witnessed in the previous 
year due to tariffs, supply chain adjustments and evolving production realignments. However, gradual improvements in 
trade linkages, resilient services trade and continued investments across technology, infrastructure, renewable energy 
and digital ecosystems are expected to support economic activity and capital flows across global markets.
Over the medium term, global growth is projected at 3.2% in CY 2027, indicating moderate but resilient economic 
expansion supported by easing supply chain disruptions and gradual normalisation in inflationary pressures. Industrial 
sectors linked to electrification, renewable energy, mobility solutions, digital infrastructure and advanced manufacturing 
are expected to witness sustained long-term growth momentum driven by increasing investments in energy transition, 
localisation initiatives and technology-led industrial expansion. At the same time, geopolitical uncertainties, elevated 
interest rates, trade policy changes and disruptions across strategic trade routes such as the Strait of Hormuz are 
expected to remain key factors influencing global business sentiment, commodity prices and industrial activity.

OUTLOOK
India’s economic outlook remains structurally strong, supported by sustained infrastructure investments, resilient 
domestic consumption, improving manufacturing competitiveness and continued policy focus on industrial expansion 
and energy transition. Real GDP growth for FY 2026-27 is projected at 6.6%5, reflecting continued momentum in 
investment activity and private sector participation. The anticipated revival in the private investment cycle, supported 
by healthier corporate balance sheets, improving credit availability and stable interest rate conditions, is expected to 
further strengthen industrial and manufacturing growth. Simultaneously, continued progress in renewable energy 
deployment, electric mobility adoption and energy storage infrastructure is expected to create long-term growth 
opportunities across industrial and technology-led sectors.
India is also expected to benefit from ongoing global supply-chain diversification and increasing integration into 
international manufacturing networks, particularly across high-technology, electronics and clean energy ecosystems. 
Government support through Viability Gap Funding (VGF), PLI schemes, infrastructure modernisation and trade 
agreements is expected to accelerate investments in advanced manufacturing and storage technologies. However, the 
near-term outlook remains exposed to risks arising from geopolitical conflicts, crude oil price volatility, evolving global 
trade regulations and supply-chain disruptions. Nevertheless, stable inflation trends, improving fiscal consolidation, 
strong banking sector fundamentals and sustained policy reforms are expected to support long-term economic 
resilience and industrial competitiveness.

INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS
Our International Automotive Business recorded meaningful progress, with Amaron, PowerZone and ELITO reaching 
customers across more than 70 countries spanning Asia Pacific, the Middle East, Africa, Europe and the Americas. Wider 
distributor coverage, entry into new markets, establishment of a local entity in the United States and expansion of the EFB 
and AGM portfolio marked important developments across the business. As start-stop systems become more prevalent and 
electrical complexity within vehicles continues to increase, demand for advanced low-voltage battery technologies is rising 
across several global markets. Our growing international presence is also a reflection of the increasing acceptance of Indian-
manufactured products across automotive replacement channels worldwide.
Global Automotive Landscape
The global automotive industry 
continues to evolve at different speeds 
across regions. Electrification remains 
a long-term trend, although adoption 
patterns continue to vary depending 
on policy frameworks, infrastructure 
readiness and consumer affordability. 
Throughout this transition, the 12V 
lead-acid battery segment has retained 
its relevance across global vehicle 
populations.
A notable development across Europe, 
the Middle East and the Americas has 
been the growing penetration of start-
stop technology. This trend is resulting 
in higher demand for advanced battery 
formats such as EFB and AGM. At the 
same time, advanced driver assistance systems, connected infotainment 
platforms and increasing onboard 
electrical loads are raising performance 
expectations from 12V battery systems.
In the United States, a growing 
population of start-stop vehicles is 
entering the replacement cycle. Across 
Europe, stringent emission regulations 
and an ageing vehicle parc continue 
to support replacement demand. 
In APAC and MEA markets, vehicle 
parc expansion, rising consumer 
aspirations and growth in organised 
retail channels are widening the 
addressable market across passenger 
and commercial vehicle categories.

The telecom energy storage market 
moved deeper into lithium-ion 
adoption during the reported financial 
year, with nearly 70% of annual 
deployments, including both new

demand. Network modernisation,

infrastructure.
The resulting chemistry shift materially 
reduced demand for lead-acid 
batteries across telecom applications.

retained combined telecom energy

preserving leadership in the lead-acid 
battery segment. We also emerged

to leading private telecom operators.

Our Strategic Priorities
Industries linked to energy and mobility are changing rapidly. Technologies 
that were once emerging are becoming commercially viable, competitive 
intensity is increasing across markets and energy storage is finding relevance 
across a much broader range of applications. As electrification gathers pace 
and energy systems become more interconnected, the boundaries between  
traditional sectors are beginning to blur.
We enter this phase from a position of strength. Over many years, we have built leading positions in automotive 
and industrial energy storage through sustained investment in technology, manufacturing capabilities and market 
development. Our strategic priorities build on these foundations. We are expanding into adjacent markets and 
applications, broadening our technology portfolio and improving execution across the organisation, while retaining 
a clear commitment to the businesses that have shaped our position over the years.
Our Strategic 
PrioritiesReachExpanding Our
LeadershipDeepening Our 
Stronger 
CoreBuilding a 
Leadership  
& CapabilityDigital & 
DataSustainability & 
GovernanceEnablersExpanding Our Deepening Our Building a 
Reach Leadership Stronger Core
The opportunities emerging across energy 
storage and mobility are not confined to 
any single market or geography. Demand 
is growing across regions, while customers 
increasingly expect shorter response times, 
local engagement and reliable supply 
arrangements. Manufacturing location, 
market access and customer proximity are 
becoming more important considerations 
in how businesses compete.
We are expanding our presence across 
priority geographies while deepening 
our engagement across existing 
markets. This includes investments in 
local manufacturing, market-specific 
partnerships and distribution networks that 
bring us closer to customers. We are also 
evaluating opportunities that can provide 
access to new markets, technologies and 
business segments.
Our objective is straightforward. We aim to 
widen our market presence, participate in a 
broader range of applications and reduce 
dependence on any single geography. 
As our footprint expands, we expect a 
more balanced business across markets, 
customers and end-use segments.Scale increases complexity. Growth across 
technologies, products and geographies 
places greater demands on manufacturing 
systems, business processes and 
organisational effectiveness. The ability to 
execute consistently therefore becomes 
an important source of competitive 
advantage.
Our efforts are directed towards 
improving productivity, quality and 
responsiveness across the organisation. 
Digital technologies, automation and 
advanced analytics are increasingly 
embedded across manufacturing and 
business processes. Smart manufacturing 
initiatives are improving throughput, 
quality and predictability across operations, 
while data-driven decision-making is 
improving planning and execution. Process 
simplification remains an important area 
of focus. Greater consistency across 
systems and workflows improves efficiency 
and allows faster responses to changing 
business requirements.
Technology partnerships also contribute 
to this effort by providing access to 
specialised expertise and reducing 
development timelines across selected 
initiatives. The objective is straightforward. 
Create an organisation that can operate 
at greater scale while maintaining 
execution discipline across businesses and 
geographies.Low-voltage energy storage remains 
central to our business. Vehicle 
architectures, energy systems and 
customer requirements continue to 
evolve, but the need for dependable low-
voltage power remains unchanged across 
automotive and industrial applications.
Our strategy is anchored in this 
opportunity. Lead-acid batteries remain 
an important part of the business and 
continue to serve large installed bases 
across multiple applications. At the 
same time, lithium-ion technologies are 
expanding into new use cases across 
mobility and energy storage. Emerging 
chemistries are also progressing across 
specific applications and markets.
Our response is not centred on a single 
technology pathway. It is centred on 
maintaining relevance across technologies, 
applications and customer requirements. 
The role of energy storage systems is 
also expanding. Battery management 
systems, power electronics, controls 
and sensing technologies now play an 
important role in monitoring battery 
performance, managing energy flows 
and improving system reliability. As a 
result, our investments extend beyond 
batteries to include battery packs, battery 
management systems and integrated 
energy solutions.
This broadens our participation across the 
value chain and improves our ability to 
address changing market requirements.

Stakeholder Engagement and Materiality Assessment
Long-term value creation depends on our ability to understand and respond 
to the expectations of stakeholders who influence and are impacted by our 
business. As we expand across energy storage, new energy technologies and 
mobility solutions, stakeholder perspectives provide important inputs into 
how we evaluate opportunities, manage risks and priorities areas of focus.
Our engagement process enables continuous dialogue with customers, employees, suppliers, investors, communities, 
regulators and industry associations. These interactions help us understand evolving expectations, industry developments and 
emerging priorities across the economic, environmental, social and governance dimensions of our business.
The insights gathered through these engagements are assessed alongside business priorities, industry trends and enterprise 
risks to identify the issues that are most relevant to our stakeholders and our long-term success.

FROM STAKEHOLDER INSIGHTS TO MATERIAL PRIORITIES
Stakeholder engagement and materiality assessment are closely linked processes. The concerns, expectations and priorities 
identified through stakeholder interactions are evaluated alongside business strategy, market developments, sustainability trends, 
regulatory requirements and enterprise risks. This enables us to identify and prioritise the environmental, social, governance and 
business matters that have the greatest relevance to our stakeholders and the organisation's long-term success.SUSTAINABILITY COMMITTEE
We have established a Sustainability Committee to define our sustainability roadmap and oversee its effective implementation. 
Chaired by the Executive Director, the Committee comprises senior leadership, including the Chief Sustainability Officer and other 
key functional heads. It provides strategic direction; reviews progress against defined sustainability goals and ensures alignment 
with regulatory requirements and global best practices. The Committee also facilitates cross-functional collaboration, enabling 
the integration of sustainability considerations into business decisions and driving accountability across the organisation.Our Materiality Approach

operational execution, manufacturing efficiency and market responsiveness, 
while our new energy business involves technology development, customer 
qualification, capacity creation and long-term capital deployment. Managing 
these priorities requires informed decision-making, clear accountability and 
oversight across a diverse set of business activities.
Our governance framework provides this through a structure by which the Board oversees strategy, risk, compliance, 
capital allocation and business performance across our operations and wholly owned subsidiaries. Supported by its 
Committees and executive leadership teams, the framework facilitates review of material matters, implementation of 
Board-approved decisions and accountability across businesses, subsidiaries and strategic initiatives.

Acknowledgement – Tubular Factory Reinstatement 
The fire incident at the Company's Tubular Battery Plant at the Amara Raja Growth Corridor on January 30, 2026 
resulted in a claim under the Company's Industrial All Risk Insurance Programme. Following completion of the 
assessment and claims process involving the Lead Insurer, Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited, the appointed 
surveyors and loss assessors, and the Company's insurance broker, Lorven Insurance Broking Services Private Limited, 
the Company received the insurance claim settlement. The Board places on record its appreciation for the cooperation 
and professional engagement of all parties associated with the assessment, recovery and settlement process.RISK GOVERNANCE
Risk management forms an integral 
part of how we evaluate opportunities, 
allocate capital and conduct our 
operations. Oversight is provided 
by the Board of Directors and the 
Risk Management Committee, which 
review material risks, mitigation 
actions and emerging developments 
that may influence the business. 
At the management level, the Risk 
Management Steering Committee 
(RMSC) periodically reviews the 
Company's risk profile and monitors 
progress on risk mitigation plans.
Risk ownership resides with the business. 
Designated risk owners across functions, divisions, subsidiaries and business 
units are responsible for identifying, 
assessing and managing risks within 
their respective areas of responsibility. 
A Risk Management Coordinator 
facilitates the risk management process, 
maintains oversight of risk reporting and 
works with risk owners to ensure that 
material risks are reviewed, monitored 
and escalated through the appropriate 
governance channels.

Occupational Health
The Company strengthened preventive

the Vitality Index to monitor the 
4Bs—Blood Pressure, Blood Sugar,

early risk identification and targeted 
health interventions. Dedicated health 
monitoring facilities and awareness 
initiatives further encouraged 
employees to proactively manage their 
well-being.
As part of our ongoing HSE 
improvement initiatives, we have fully 
equipped Occupational Health Centers 
(OHCs) across all facilities with modern 
infrastructure and medical equipment. 
These facilities have improved 
diagnostic accuracy, strengthened 
emergency preparedness, and elevated 
the overall quality of employee care, 
ensuring alignment with the latest 
occupational health standards.

strengthened its proactive safety

downtime while enhancing electrical 
and plant safety.

on technology interventions across

Advanced lead-acid technologies

delivers reliable power performance, improved power-to-weight characteristics

supporting improved reliability and 
performance requirements.

additive formulations for improving 
industrial battery performance and 
development of methodologies aimed at 
improving state-of-charge performance 
in two-wheeler batteries.

MANUFACTURING AND 
PROCESS ENGINEERING
Manufacturing and process 
engineering initiatives during  
FY 2025-26 remained focused on 
improving product durability, process 
reliability, throughput and energy 
efficiency across battery manufacturing 
operations. Advanced curing 
techniques were introduced across 
four-wheeler and UPS applications 
to enhance plate robustness. New 
processes and compatible material 
systems were also implemented to 
improve mechanical strength and 
durability in commercial batteries.
The year also saw integration of 
engineered fibre into electrodes 
to improve structural integrity. In 
automotive applications, durable and 
sustainable AGM separator solutions 
were introduced to support product 
performance and reliability requirements.
Process optimisation initiatives 
were undertaken across multiple 
manufacturing stages. Advanced and 
energy-efficient formation equipment 
was implemented in the tubular battery 
plant, while premix expander systems 
were introduced to improve sustainable 
productivity in flooded Home UPS 
battery manufacturing. Formation 
process cycle times in AGM batteries 
were also optimised to improve 
throughput and operational efficiency.

team comprising 300+ professionals with cumulative industry expertise of

OUR PEOPLE STRATEGY
Our ‘People Strategy Model’ provides 
a structured approach to attracting, 
engaging, developing and enabling 
talent in line with the organisation’s 
evolving business priorities. The 
framework brings together workforce 
capability, leadership development, 
employee engagement and wellbeing 
to strengthen organisational readiness 
across levels while creating stronger

The ‘Talent Management Model’ 
translates this approach into action 
through structured learning initiatives, 
leadership programmes, accelerated 
career pathways and digital learning 
platforms. 
Workforce Planning and Performance Alignment
Workforce planning aligns business priorities, operating requirements and organisational capabilities with current and future 
talent needs. The process incorporates environmental assessment, workforce analysis and cross-functional review to identify 
capability requirements across businesses and functions. Approved workforce plans are implemented across the organisation 
and monitored periodically to assess progress, respond to changing business requirements and maintain alignment with 
organisational objectives.

ENABLEDPerformance Management and Organisational Accountability
Our digital Performance Management System (PMS) aligns organisational priorities with individual goals, behavioural 
expectations and development objectives. We have introduced an Accountability Scorecard Framework that integrates the 
PMS framework by linking organisational objectives, Key Result Areas (KRAs), Balanced Scorecards (BSC), Objectives, Actions 
and Targets (OATs), leadership behaviours and development inputs into a structured performance assessment process.
The framework recognises both business outcomes and the manner in which those outcomes are delivered. A fully automated 
PMS enables real-time check-ins, continuous feedback and structured developmental conversations between managers and 
employees, improving the quality and frequency of performance discussions across levels.

=== page 66 ===
WATER AND TREATED 
WATER MANAGEMENT 
During the year, multi-parameter online 
wastewater analyzers were installed at 
the STP and ETP units to enable 24×7 
real-time monitoring of key effluent 
quality parameters. The system is 
integrated with a centralized digital 
dashboard and transmits data directly 
to the Pollution Control Board (PCB) 
server, strengthening process control, 
regulatory compliance, and timely 
corrective action.
We have installed Effluent Treatment 
Plants (ETPs) at all units to manage 
wastewater from production 
processes. To ensure complete 
reuse, Zero Liquid Discharge 
(ZLD) systems with capacities of 
280 KLD and 500 KLD have been 
implemented. These ZLD plants 
feature a pretreatment system 
for hardness reduction, followed 
by Reverse Osmosis process, and 
further treatment using a Multiple 
Effect Evaporator (MEE) and 
Agitated Thin Film Dryer (ATFD).In-house sewage treatment facilities 
with reuse water pools enable the reuse 
of treated wastewater for horticulture. 
A 14,500 kL stormwater collection pond 
and dedicated rainwater treatment 
plant facilitate the capture, treatment, 
and reuse of rainwater for laundry 
operations.
The Company has also constructed 
check dams across the Chittoor and 
Tirupati districts with a combined 
storage capacity of 1,433,260 kL, 
enabling the harvesting of 8,600,025 
kL of rainwater. In addition, internal 
ponds with a total capacity of 
559,758 kL facilitate the collection of 
a further 2,244,836 kL of rainwater, 
strengthening groundwater recharge 
and local water availability.
To reinforce transparency and 
credibility, Bureau Veritas India Private 
Ltd. independently verified all check 
dams and ponds and confirmed a total 
groundwater recharge of 10,844,861 
kL during FY2025. Based on desktop 
reviews, site verification, and stakeholder interactions, the Company achieved a 
Water Positivity Ratio of 11.94. In FY 2026-27, we have planned initiatives to reduce 
sludge and salt moisture percentage at ETP to minimise waste load and disposal 
cost.

AIR EMISSIONS 
As part of its commitment to 
environmental sustainability, the 
Company has deployed advanced air 
pollution control systems to effectively 
manage process emissions. Dust 
extraction systems with bag filters are 
installed in the pasting and assembly 
areas, while fume extraction systems 
with scrubbers operate in the grid 
casting and formation sections. These 
systems are routinely validated, and 
emission stacks are monitored quarterly 
to ensure regulatory compliance and 
optimal performance.
During the year, ultrasonic flowmeters 
were installed in the Assembly Line 
Dust Extraction (DE) system to enable 
real-time monitoring of temperature, 
velocity, and volumetric flow. Integrated 
with a centralized digital dashboard, 
the system provides continuous 
visibility of dust extraction performance 
across all assembly lines and enables 
prompt corrective action in the event of 
any performance deviation.
A Continuous Emission Monitoring 
System (CEMS) has been installed 
on the stacks of the Pasting Area 
to continuously monitor particulate 
emissions, with real-time data 
automatically transmitted to the 
Pollution Control Board (PCB) server, 
enabling continuous compliance and 
timely corrective action.ENERGY AND CARBON 
We maintain a strong and disciplined 
approach to carbon emissions 
management, aligned with the 
Greenhouse Gas Protocol and ISO 
14064 standards. Our strategy is driven 
by targeted decarbonization initiatives 
and continuous improvements in 
energy efficiency.
Sustainability remains integral to our 
growth, reflected in the increasing 
integration of renewable energy—
particularly solar—into our operations. 
With ISO 50001:2018 certification across 
all facilities, we demonstrate robust 
and systematic energy management 
practices.
Our 67 MW of captive renewable 
energy capacity now contributes 
21.82% to our overall energy mix, 
enabling us to avoid 73,831 tCO₂e of 
carbon emissions during the year.
Our energy monitoring system 
continues to serve as a critical digital 
enabler, enhancing operational 
efficiency through real-time tracking of energy consumption and timely 
corrective actions. Introduced to 
replace manual, labor-intensive data 
collection, the system streamlines data 
acquisition from over 2,000 energy 
meters and enables precise monitoring 
of more than 700 Energy Performance 
Indicators (EnPIs).

BIODIVERSITY
ARE&M is committed to nature-
based solutions that drive 
environmental sustainability. Our 
ongoing tree plantation initiatives 
strengthen green cover within and 
around our facilities, supporting 
biodiversity, ecosystem health, 
carbon sequestration and air quality. 
Currently, 55% of our operational 
areas are under green cover, with 
over 83,576 saplings planted on-
site and an additional 72,750 in 
surrounding communities.
During the year, A structured 
biodiversity study has been 
conducted with systematic baseline 
surveys and impact assessments 
of the ecological environment 
within and surrounding our 
plants, typically covering a 10 km 
radius. Surveys documented plant 
species composition (flora), wildlife 
including birds, mammals, reptiles, 
and invertebrates (fauna) and the 
health of any nearby water bodies. 
The study was carried out by 
independent, certified ecologists, 
resulting in an assessment of ARE 
& M biodiversity impacts and the 
development of a Biodiversity 
Management Plan (BMP). The 
BMP aims to mitigate the effects 
of operational activities on local 
biodiversity, with the objective of 
achieving No Net Loss (NNL).CIRCULAR ECONOMY
ARE&M advances circular economy 
principles through robust Extended 
Producer Responsibility (EPR) 
programmes for used batteries, plastic 
waste, and e-waste, in partnership with 
authorised recyclers and collection 
agencies. During the year, 88.27% of 
the Company's lead and lead alloy 
inputs comprised secondary recycled 
material. To further strengthen 
resource circularity, the Company 
has established Amara Raja Circular 
Solutions (ARCS), a wholly owned 
subsidiary developing a state-of-the-
art battery recycling facility at Cheyyar, 
Tamil Nadu, designed for a recycling 
capacity of 150,000 MT per annum 
when fully operational.State-of-the-art 
air pollution control systems effectively 
capture and remove process fumes 
and dust. In addition, a Zero Liquid 
Discharge (ZLD) system ensures 100% 
recycling of treated water back into 
operations, reflecting ARCS’s strong 
commitment to water stewardship.
During the year, the Company achieved 
Zero Waste to Landfill (ZWTL) status for FY2026 and was awarded Platinum 
Certification by Bureau Veritas, covering 
ETP sludge and ZLD MEE/ATFD salts. 
More than 95% of these wastes 
were diverted from landfill through 
conversion for coprocessing, with the 
achievement independently verified 
through a robust, traceable, and 
auditable certification process.
PRODUCT STEWARDSHIP
ARE&M actively implements Extended 
Producer Responsibility (EPR) for used 
batteries, plastic waste, and e-waste 
through authorised recyclers and 
collection agencies, strengthening circularity and regulatory compliance. 
During the year, the Company 
completed Life Cycle Assessments 
(LCA) for 50% of its automotive and 
industrial SKUs to enhance product 
sustainability and resource efficiency. 
It also initiated trials to replace 
virgin plastic packaging for industrial 
batteries with compostable alternatives, 
demonstrating the potential to 
significantly reduce conventional plastic 
consumption across battery packaging.

distances ranging from 30 kilometres 
to 3,200 kilometres. This scale requires 
continuous coordination between 
logistics partners, distribution centres 
and customer-facing teams to ensure 
timely product availability.
Distribution Infrastructure
Distribution infrastructure remains an 
important component of our market 
responsiveness framework. A network of 
36 distribution points facilitates inventory 
deployment and product movement 
across markets. These facilities work 
in conjunction with branches, channel 
partners and transportation providers 
to improve product accessibility and 
fulfilment efficiency.
In addition to the distribution network, 
a dedicated Lubes Central Distribution 
Centre manages lubricant distribution 
requirements and improves inventory 
management across product categories. 
The distribution framework also 
supports export activities spanning 75 
destinations and import operations 
covering 18 locations. These capabilities 
contribute to wider market access while 
helping maintain service levels across 
domestic and international markets.
Improving Visibility Across 
Logistics Operations
Visibility across logistics activities 
remains an important requirement 
for maintaining delivery reliability 
and customer responsiveness. During 
FY 2025-26, we expanded the use of 
digital systems to improve monitoring 
and coordination across transportation 
and distribution activities.
Electronic Proof of Delivery (e-PoD) 
systems provide greater visibility 
into delivery status and material 
movement. Integration with customer 
relationship management systems 
has improved information availability 
while creating faster communication 
channels for customer-facing teams. 
These measures have also reduced 
operational risks associated with theft, 
pilferage and delivery disputes.
Reverse logistics systems have also 
been strengthened to improve 
collection efficiency and management 
of return flows across the distribution 
network. These systems contribute 
to better material traceability while 
improving coordination between 
collection points, distribution centres 
and recovery processes.
The year also saw wider deployment of 
supply chain visibility tools, warehouse management practices and planning 
systems aimed at improving inventory 
visibility and coordination across 
logistics operations. These measures 
contribute to faster decision-making 
and more effective deployment of 
inventory across markets.
Transportation Efficiency
The movement of products across 
a large geographical footprint 
requires continuous optimisation of 
transportation resources. During FY 
2025-26, we increased the deployment 
of higher-tonnage vehicles within 
transportation operations. This 
approach improved vehicle utilisation 
and transportation efficiency while 
helping optimise freight movement 
across key routes.
Transportation planning also 
incorporated multimodal logistics 
capabilities, allowing movement through 
road, rail, maritime and air networks 
based on operational requirements and 
customer needs. The flexibility offered 
by these arrangements contributes 
to continuity of supply and delivery 
reliability across markets.
Driver Welfare and Safety
Drivers and logistics support 
personnel remain an integral part 
of our distribution network. We 
conduct regular health, safety and 
environmental awareness programmes 
for drivers and janitorial communities 
associated with logistics operations. 
These programmes address safe 
driving practices, health awareness and 
environmental considerations relevant 
to transportation activities.
An in-house amenity centre provides 
drivers with facilities for rest and 
recuperation during long-distance 
transportation assignments. The facility 
offers a dedicated space where drivers 
can recover between journeys and 
access basic amenities during transit.
The combination of awareness 
programmes and welfare facilities 
has contributed to lower accident 
rates, reduced transit damage and 
improved delivery reliability across 
transportation operations.
Sustainable Sourcing and Supply 
Chain
Engaging our suppliers in sustainability 
initiatives is fundamental to achieving 
shared long-term value and advancing 
our collective sustainability ambitions. Our The event brought together our key 
supplier partners from across the globe to 
collaborate on innovative solutions aimed 
at reducing our collective environmental 
footprint and building more resilient 
and responsible supply chains. We were 
encouraged by the strong participation 
and commitments demonstrated by our 
suppliers, who share our vision for a more 
sustainable future. The summit provided 
a dynamic platform for exchanging ideas, 
setting ambitious goals and deepening 
partnerships centered around common 
sustainability priorities.
The awards presented during the summit 
recognised the significant contributions of 
our vendor partners towards advancing 
Amara Raja’s sustainability objectives, while 
also reinforcing clear expectations and 
aspirations for the future.
Additionally, during the year, we 
expanded our sustainability outreach 
to our downstream franchisee partners. 
Our engagement initiatives included 
the launch of a Franchise Sustainability 
Manual focused on ten key sustainability 
elements, alongside capability-building 
programmes, sustainability assessments and 
implementation of improvement action plans.

Responsible Logistics
Environmental considerations are 
increasingly incorporated into 
transportation and distribution 
activities. During FY 2025-26, EV and 
CNG vehicles were introduced within 
transportation operations as part of 
efforts to reduce the environmental 
footprint associated with logistics 
activities. Pilot deployment of solar 
installations was also initiated at 
selected distribution centres, with 
a phased rollout planned across 
additional locations.
COMMUNITIES
Our community investments 
are directed towards areas that 
influence educational attainment, 
employability, healthcare access, 
water availability and quality of life 
within neighbouring communities. 
These interventions are undertaken 
through Rajanna Foundation and 
Amara Raja Educational Society 
(ARES), with programmes designed 
to address long-term developmental 
priorities across the regions where 
we operate.
Many of the communities surrounding 
our facilities are located in rural and 
semi-rural areas where access to quality 
education, healthcare, skill development 
and essential infrastructure remains 
uneven. Our approach seeks to improve 
access to opportunities, strengthen 
community infrastructure and create 
conditions that contribute to social 
and economic participation. Impact 
assessments conducted during the 
year provide insight into how these 
programmes are influencing educational 
outcomes, employability, healthcare 
access and community well-being.
Reverse Logistics and 
Regulatory Compliance
Battery collection and recovery activities 
require close coordination across 
customers, channel partners, collection 
centres and logistics providers. We 
manage battery collection and reverse 
logistics activities in accordance with 
the Battery Waste Management Rules 
(BWMR), 2022. The system facilitates 
the collection of BWMR stock as well as 
warranty-return stock through established 
collection and transportation mechanisms.
Collection, transportation and recovery 
activities are integrated into our reverse logistics framework, improving traceability 
and ensuring responsible handling of used 
batteries. These processes also contribute 
to regulatory compliance requirements 
relating to battery collection and recycling.
During FY 2025-26, we were among the 
few organisations to successfully achieve 
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) 
targets under the applicable regulatory 
framework. The achievement reflects 
effective coordination across collection 
systems, channel networks and reverse 
logistics operations.
Education and Academic Access
Education remains one of the most 
important contributors to long-term 
social mobility. Through Rajanna 
Foundation, we provide access to 
quality education for students from 
rural communities while creating 
pathways for higher education and 
future employment opportunities.
Our schools serve students drawn 
primarily from neighbouring villages, 
many of whom are first-generation 
learners. Impact assessment findings 
indicate improvements in attendance, 
classroom engagement and 
conceptual understanding, supported 
by access to digital learning tools, 
transport facilities and a structured 
academic environment. These 
institutions continue to expand access 
to education for students who may 
otherwise have limited access to 
quality schooling.

conservation infrastructure.

Employee cost increased owing to head count addition for new plants and incrementsDuring the year under review, other income decreased primarily due to lower income from mutual funds, as

exchange gains.

due to higher volumes of Lubes, storage batteries and Home UPS in the current financial year.During the year under review, sale of products was higher as compared to the previous year, primarily due to

5. Subsidiaries and Consolidated Financial 
Statements
 a. Subsidiary Companies: During the year under 
review, the Company has four wholly owned 
subsidiaries. Details of the wholly owned subsidiaries 
are given as under:
  i. Amara Raja Batteries Middle East (FZE) 
(‘ARBME’), Sharjah, UAE, a wholly owned 
subsidiary of the Company, reported a net 
revenue	of	₹	15.84	crores	with	a	Profit	After	Tax	
of	₹	1.19	crores for FY26.
  ii. Amara Raja Circular Solutions Private 
Limited (ARCS), Andhra Pradesh, India a 
wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, is 
establishing a state-of-the-art battery recycling 
facility at Cheyyar, Tamil Nadu, as a key 
component of the Company’s circular economy 
and sustainable supply chain strategy. The 
facility is expected to play a significant role 
in meeting the Company's lead and alloy 
requirements	 through	 environmentally	
responsible recycling operations.
   During the year, ARCS successfully commenced 
Battery Breaker operations and is currently in 
the ramp-up phase. Refining operations, which 
commenced during the second half of 2024, 
continue to scale up, while the integration of 
scrap battery processing through to lead ingot 
production is progress ing as planned.
   The Company is also undertaking Phase 
II refinery expansion at the facility, with 
commissioning targeted by 2027. In addition, 
commissioning of the Crystallizer and De-
sulphurisation plant is expected shortly. 
The de-sulphurisation technology, a first-
of-its-kind application in India for battery 
recycling, is expected to improve lead recovery 
yields, reduce waste generation, and enable 
the production of Sodium Sulphate as a 
valuable by-product.
   The plant has been designed in accordance with 
global standards and incorporates advanced 
automation across the recycling value chain, 
from battery feeding and breaking to robotic ingot stacking. ARCS continues to focus on 
increasing the proportion of alloy production, 
with plans to ramp up alloy volumes during 
FY27, thereby enhancing value addition 
and profitability.
	 	 	 For	 FY26,	ARCS	reported	net	revenue	of	₹	1,456.36	
crores and a profit after tax of ₹	21.50	crores.
  iii. Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies 
Private Limited (ARACT), Telangana, India 
is a wholly owned material subsidiary of the 
Company in terms of Regulation 16(1)(c) of the 
Listing Regulations. ARACT continued to make 
significant progress in establishing domestic 
capabilities across advanced lithium-ion cell 
and battery pack manufacturing during FY26. 
The business transitioned from capability 
creation to execution readiness, supported 
by continued investments in manufacturing 
infrastructure, Research & Development, 
customer engagement and supply chain 
development. The Pack Assembly Plant 
expanded its customer base in the Energy 
Storage Systems (ESS) segment and continued 
operational ramp-up towards a targeted annual 
supply capacity of 1.5 GWh and strengthened 
EV battery pack manufacturin g capabilities.
   ARACT is in the process of commissioning 
its Customer Qualification Plant (CQP) with 
cylindrical and prismatic cell manufacturing 
lines, marking an important milestone towards 
operational readiness and customer validation. 
The e+ Energy Labs in Hyderabad also is in 
the process of completion as an integrated 
research and innovation hub for advanced 
battery technologies. Construction activities 
at the Amara Raja Giga Corridor, Divitipally, 
Telangana also progressed substantially, with 
structural development and procurement of 
key	process	equipment	 advancing	in	line	with	
project timelines. The Company continued to 
strengthen its integrated New Energy platform 
spanning electric mobility solutions, stationary 
energy storage systems and advanced cell 
technologies, with Start of Production (SoP) for 
lithium-ion cell manufacturing planned for 2027. 
   For FY26, ARACT report ed revenues of  
₹	786.51	crores,	while	posting a net loss of  
₹	73.23	crores,	reflecting	the	early-stage	 nature	
of the investments and ongoing ramp-up in 
manufacturing infrastructure.
=== page 83 ===
Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Limited156
  iv. Amara Raja Power Systems Limited 
(‘ARPS’), Andhra Pradesh, India, a wholly-
owned subsidiary of the Company, continued 
to strengthen its presence across industrial 
chargers, integrated power systems, EV charging 
solutions, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) 
and Home Energy applications during FY26. 
The business recorded improved commercial 
traction in DC fast charging solutions, expanding 
its customer base across Charge Point Operators 
(CPOs), infrastructure developers and OEMs, 
supported by increased order inflows and 
localisation initiatives aligned with Phased 
Manufacturing Programme (PMP) guidelines.
   During the year, ARPS also advanced its Home 
Energy portfolio through development of 
lithium-based Home UPS (HUPS) systems and 
hybrid inverter platforms for residential and 
small commercial applications. Prototype models 
and pilot deployments were undertaken to 
support field validation and phased commercial 
readiness.	ARPS	reported	net	revenue	of	₹149.32	
crores	with	a	loss	of	₹	20.69	crores for FY26.

18. Risk Management 
 The Board has constituted a Risk Management Committee, 
pursuant to the Regulation 21 of Listing Regulations, to 
periodically review the risks associated with the Company’s 
business, ensure that appropriate methodology, 
processes and systems are in place for review of such 
risks, formulate the risk management policy and oversee 
its implementation. The Corporate Governance Report, 
forming part of this Annual Report, details the Committee's 
composition, meetings, attendance of its members at such 
meetings, the Committee’s terms of reference, etc.
 The Company has an elaborate Risk Management 
framework in place, which helps identify and mitigate 
risks. Such framework lays down the procedure for 
risk identification, assessment and mitigation through 
the internal Risk Management Steering Committee 
which reports to the Risk Management Committee on a 
periodic basis.
 The major risks, including financial, operational, sectoral, 
sustainability (particularly ESG-related risks), information, 
and cyber security risks, identified by the businesses and 
functions are systematically addressed through mitigating 
actions on a co ntinuing basis.
 During the year, the Committee, inter alia , reviewed the 
Enterprise Risk Management framework, including risk 
governance, risk assessment processes, and reporting 
and communication mechanisms of the Company and its 
wholly owned subsidiaries. The Committee reviewed the 
key risks along with the risk indicators, risk ratings, risk 
appetite and adopted suitable risk mit igation plans. 
 The Company conducted extensive trainings and 
awareness sessions for employees of various grades to 
inculcate culture of risk management within the Company
 In the opinion of the Board, there are no major risks 
that have the potential to threaten the existence 
of the Company.

 The Company has established a whistle-blower policy/

 g. Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) 
  Section 124 of the Act read with IEPF (Accounting, 
Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016, mandates 
that	the	companies	are	required	to	transfer	dividend	
that has remained unclaimed and unpaid for a period 
of seven years from the unpaid dividend account to 
the IEPF. Further, the Rules mandate that the shares 
on which dividend remains unpaid or unclaimed for 
seven consecutive years or more be transferred to 
the Demat account of the IEPF Authority.
  The details relating to the amount of unclaimed 
dividend transferred to the IEPF and the shares 
transferred to the Demat account of the IEPF 
Authority during FY26 and due for transfer in FY27 
are provided in the Corporate Governance Report 
which forms part of this Annual Report. The Company has issued individual notices to the members whose 
dividend is unclaimed and unpaid, advising them to 
claim	their	dividend.	Shareholders	 are	requested	to	
ensure their dividends are claimed on time. In case 
of non-encashment of dividends, shareholders are 
advised to approach the Company or Registrar and 
Transfer Agent to claim their uncla imed dividends.

 Board Meetings, Procedure & Term of Board 
Membership
 The Company plans and prepares the schedule of Board 
and Committee meetings in advance. The Board meets at 
least	once	a	quarter	to	review	the	quarterly	results	and	
other	items	as	required.	Additional	meetings	are	held	
when necessary. Input and feedback of Board members 
are taken and considered while preparing the agenda and 
documents for the Board meetings. Agenda and other 
related information are circulated to directors well in 
advance of the meetings. At these meetings, directors can 
provide their input and suggestions on various strategic 
and operational matters. The meeting schedule and 
agenda are finalised in consultation with the Chairperson 
of the Board and of the respectiv e Committee(s).
 During the year, majority of the Board meetings were held 
through video conference as per the provisions of law. The 
Board met five (5) times, complying with the applicable statutory	requirements.	 Details	of	the	attendance	 of	
Directors at the Board Meetings / AGM held during the 
year are given in Table 3. In addition, an annual meet 
of Board of Directors, along with Management teams, 
was held to discuss Stratlign of Company and its Wholly 
Owned Subsidiaries (ARACT, ARCS, ARPS and ARBME).
 A detailed presentation is made at each Board Meeting, 
covering highlights and performances of the business. 
The Board reviews the items on the agenda, particularly 
quarterly	financial	results,	annual	financial	statements,	
annual operating plans and budgets, capital budgets, 
investments, statement of significant transactions etc., 
of the Company and its Wholly Owned Subsidiaries. The 
compliance reports of laws applicable to the Company, 
minutes of the Committee meetings, and a summary 
of Board minutes of the Wholly Owned Subsidiaries 
are placed before the Board for review/noting. Other 
significant details included in the presentation/agenda 
discussion cover occurrences, any material effluent 
or pollution problems, material default in financial 
obligations, public or product liability claims, related party 
transactions, borrowings, updates on internal controls 
including internal financial controls, Cybersecurity & 
Information Technology updates and Sustainability 
& ESG updates, data protection laws, information on 
succession planning and structured leadership pipeline, 
risk analysis of various products, markets and businesses, 
risk refresh update, detailed analysis of potential 
acquisition	 targets	and	possible	divestments,	 details	of	
any joint venture or collaboration agreements including 
technical collaborations, contracts/arrangements in which 
director(s) are interested, materially important show 
cause, demand, prosecution and penalty n otices, if any.
 The important decisions taken/suggestions made by 
the Board and/or Committees at their meetings are 
communicated to the respective departments. Action 
taken/status reports on decisions/suggestions of the 
previous meeting(s) are followed up and placed at the 
next meeting. During the year under review, the Board has 
accepted all the recommendations/submissions from all 
the Committees.

the Company and it s subsidiaries.
 A three-day long Annual Board Meet was held in

 Board Evaluation
 During the year, the Board carried out an annual 
performance evaluation of the Board, its Committees and 
individual Directors, including the Chairman, in accordance 
with the applicable provisions of the Act and the Listing 
Regulations. The evaluation process was conducted 
internally through structured feedback obtained from all 
Directors, covering peer evaluation and the effectiveness 
of the Board and its Committees. The exercise focused 
on enhancing the overall effectiveness of the Board and 
strengthening governance practices with in the Company. The performance evaluation of the Board was carried out 
with reference to its structure, composition, governance 
and overall functioning, including its effectiveness in 
guiding corporate strategy, reviewing business plans 
and budgets, overseeing risk management, internal 
controls, financial reporting and statutory compliances, 
and ensuring effective information flow and decision-
making processes.
 The Committees of the Board were evaluated on the 
effective discharge of their roles and responsibilities in 
accordance with their respective terms of reference and 
powers delegated by the Board. The Audit Committee’s 
evaluation covered oversight of financial reporting 
and statements, related party transactions, internal 
financial controls, risk management systems, compliance 
with applicable laws, and its effectiveness in auditor 
appointment, performance review, audit planning, report 
review, and regulatory compliance. The Nomination and 
Remuneration Committee, Corporate Social Responsibility 
Committee, and Stakeholders’ Relationship Committee 
were assessed on the effectiveness of their functioning 
and discharge of responsibilities. The Risk Management 
Committee was evaluated on the exercise of delegated 
powers and its contribution to governance, risk oversight 
and d ecision-making.
 The Chairman was evaluated on leadership effectiveness, 
governance practices and facilitating participation of 
Directors, while Individual Directors were assessed on 
their participation, domain expertise and understanding 
of governance and regulatory matters. The performance 
evaluation of all Directors, including Independent 
Directors, was carried out by the entire Board, excluding 
the Director being evaluated. The contribution and 
impact of individual members were evaluated on several 
parameters, such as level of engagement, independence 
of judgment, conflict resolution, contributions to enhance 
the Board’s overall effectiveness, etc. Feedback including 
positive attributes and improvement areas, if any, for each 
director were provided to him/her on a confidential basis. 
During their executive sessions, the Independent Directors 
separately evaluated the performance of the Board as a 
whole, the Chairman and the Non-Indepen dent Directors.
 The conclusions of the evaluation exercise were noted by 
the Board at its meeting. The Board concluded that the 
Board, its Committees and the Directors continued to 
function effectively in the discharge of their respective 
responsibilities.
